name: Deleting a repo's only GitHub token warns first, then leaves it broken but readable
description: Modeled on 02/04/07: navigate to the seeded repo's settings page and confirm the seeded `demo` token's label is shown; go to Settings → GitHub Tokens and confirm it lists with a repo count of 1; delete it and confirm the orphan warning names 1 repository before the second click actually deletes; back on the repo's PR list, confirm the amber 'no token' badge appears and the seeded PR #482 stays visible — the local-first guarantee. Scoped to what is reachable offline: reassigning a token would call POST /repos/:id/github-token → probeToken → listPullRequests, which needs a resolvable PAT and live GitHub access that e2e/ deliberately has neither of (see e2e/INSIGHTS.md), so that half of the flow is verified manually against real GitHub instead. Assumes a freshly-seeded DB where acme/payments-api is the only repo and its github_token_id points at the seeded `demo` token — guaranteed by the e2e-web.yml workflow's fresh seed; run locally against a clean DB (see e2e/README.md).

steps.label: root redirects to the seeded repo's PR list
open the repo settings page via the sidebar nav
repo settings page renders the token section
the seeded token's label is shown on the repo settings page
the token shows a repo count of 1

cmd: 1 repository will be left without a token
steps.label: the orphan warning names 1 repository before any deletion happens
return to the repo's PR list via the sidebar nav
the amber 'no token' badge appears now that the repo has no token

cmd: Add rate limiting to public API endpoints
steps.label: the seeded PR stays readable despite the broken token (local-first)
